## Result

`output_evaluation.json` written and validated: `VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric20-semantic`.

**Score: 84/88 — fixed 95.5% (denominator 88), normalized 95.5% (denominator 88).** No questions were N/A, so both bases coincide and `excluded_max_points` is 0. Every one of the 20 items carries an explicit `applicable: true`; the five conditional items (Q8, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q13, Q15, Q17) each record `applicability_evidence` drawn from *other* questions' fields, per the anti-circular rule — Q11's gate, for instance, rests on `external_resources` (Q14) linking github.com/AI-READI, not on its own strategy fields.

Deductions: Q1=4 (three named slots empty — `resources`, `parent_datasets`, `regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level` — though content exists under adjacent names), Q11=4 (strategies comprehensive but no tool versions or repository pinned to any conversion), Q13=4 (v2.0.0 unreachable despite holding its own DOI; no preservation commitment beyond the project period), Q19=4 (lineage complete in text but entities, activities and agents are unlinked across four sections).

Two things worth flagging in the semantic layer. First, the record's arithmetic is independently verifiable and holds exactly: subcrate file counts sum to 356,334 against a declared 356,343, the shortfall being precisely the nine root CDS metadata files that `notes` enumerates; per-collection bytes land within ~410 KB of `total_size_bytes`, exactly as its `source_caveats` predicts. That corroboration drove several 5s that would otherwise rest on assertion alone.

Second, three failed consistency checks are substantive rather than cosmetic. The de-identification account is self-contradictory — "no identifiers were collected, so none was necessary" and "stripped of PHI via Safe Harbor" cannot both describe the same release. The PI's affiliation asserts Washington University in St. Louis while the record's own RePORTER note names University of Washington as grantee; these are distinct institutions, and the tier-ranking rule appears to have propagated an upstream name collision rather than resolved it. And no DPIA exists despite `participant_privacy.reidentification_risk` conceding an identification pathway. In each case the datasheet surfaces the tension in `source_caveats` instead of concealing it, which is why the affected items retained their bands with the defects logged separately — the failures are in the underlying sources, not in the documentation's candour.

Two caveats on method: `shasum` and ad-hoc `python3` were denied by the sandbox, so the three hashes in `metadata` are the values you supplied rather than ones I recomputed, and the arithmetic cross-checks above were done by hand. I did confirm `input/record.yaml` matches the pinned record before scoring.
